hints: Use the form $A/x+B/(2x+3)$ and clear the denominator $x(2x+3)$.
Substitute convenient values such as $x=0$ and $x=-3/2$ to determine the constants.
walkthrough:
State the partial fraction decomposition form for linear factors:
$$\dfrac{1}{x(2x + 3)} = \dfrac{A}{x} + \dfrac{B}{2x + 3}$$

Clear fractions by multiplying both sides by the denominator $x(2x + 3)$:
$$1 = A(2x + 3) + Bx$$

Determine the constant $A$ by substituting $x = 0$:
$$1 = A(2(0) + 3) + B(0) = 3A \implies A = \dfrac{1}{3}$$

Determine the constant $B$ by substituting $x = -\dfrac{3}{2}$:
$$1 = A\left(2\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right) + 3\right) + B\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = 0 - \dfrac{3}{2}B \implies B = -\dfrac{2}{3}$$

Write the final partial fraction decomposition:
$$\dfrac{1}{x(2x + 3)} = \dfrac{1}{3x} - \dfrac{2}{3(2x + 3)}$$

ai_rubric.Partial Fractions: Derives $A=\frac13$ and $B=-\frac23$, or equivalent. Concludes with $\frac1{x(2x+3)}=\frac1{3x}-\frac2{3(2x+3)}$.

hints: Insert the partial fractions from part (i) and integrate both logarithmic terms.
Use $y=1$ at $x=1$ to determine the constant before substituting $x=9$.
Exponentiate carefully and round the requested value of $y$ to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Separate the variables in the differential equation $x(2x + 3)\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = y$:
$$\dfrac{1}{y}\,\mathrm{d}y = \dfrac{1}{x(2x + 3)}\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Substitute the partial fractions found in part (i) into the right-hand integral:
$$\int \dfrac{1}{y}\,\mathrm{d}y = \int \left(\dfrac{1}{3x} - \dfrac{2}{3(2x + 3)}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Integrate each term (using $\int \dfrac{1}{2x + 3}\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(2x + 3)$):
$$\ln y = \dfrac{1}{3}\ln x - \dfrac{2}{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\ln(2x + 3)\right) + C$$
$$\ln y = \dfrac{1}{3}\ln x - \dfrac{1}{3}\ln(2x + 3) + C$$

Apply the initial boundary condition $y = 1$ when $x = 1$ to determine the constant $C$:
$$\ln 1 = \dfrac{1}{3}\ln 1 - \dfrac{1}{3}\ln(2(1) + 3) + C$$
$$0 = 0 - \dfrac{1}{3}\ln 5 + C \implies C = \dfrac{1}{3}\ln 5$$

Substitute $C$ back and combine logarithms:
$$\ln y = \dfrac{1}{3}\ln x - \dfrac{1}{3}\ln(2x + 3) + \dfrac{1}{3}\ln 5 = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(\ln\left(\dfrac{5x}{2x + 3}\right)\right)$$
$$3\ln y = \ln\left(\dfrac{5x}{2x + 3}\right) \implies \ln(y^3) = \ln\left(\dfrac{5x}{2x + 3}\right)$$
$$y^3 = \dfrac{5x}{2x + 3} \implies y = \left(\dfrac{5x}{2x + 3}\right)^{1/3}$$

State the final value rounded to 3 significant figures:
$$y = 1.29$$

ai_rubric.Solving Separable Differential Equations: Separates variables and integrates one side. Derives term $\ln y$. The final result is $\ln y=\frac13\ln x-\frac13\ln(2x+3)+\frac13\ln5$, so $y=\left(\frac{5x}{2x+3}\right)^{1/3}$ and $y(9)=1.29$.
